summary_1line: Vrihaspati describes signs of wicked people, then Bhishma recounts a sage teaching a dispossessed king that all possessions are transient and grief is futile.

image_candidates.scene_text: A jealous courtier bites his lip and shakes his head while others praise a virtuous man in a royal hall.
The ruined prince Kshemadarsin bows before the austere sage Kalakavrikshiya in a forest hermitage, confessing the loss of his kingdom.
The sage calmly teaching the prince beside a quiet forest fire, gesturing as he speaks about the fleeting nature of all possessions.
